title: Japchae
subtitle: Korean glass noodles stir-fried with vegetables and beef
excerpt: Japchae (잡채) is a Korean dish of sweet potato glass noodles stir-fried with colourful vegetables, beef, and a sweet soy and sesame dressing. Each ingredient is cooked separately to preserve its colour and texture, then combined. It is served as a side dish or main and is a staple of Korean celebrations.
sourceNotes: Japchae was created in the court of the Joseon Dynasty king Gwanghaegun in the early 17th century. The original version did not contain noodles; it was a mixture of vegetables. Dangmyeon (sweet potato glass noodles) were added later and became the defining component. The dish remains central to Korean celebrations, birthdays, and holidays.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Japchae can be made up to 2 days ahead and served at room temperature. Add a little sesame oil and toss before serving.

content.text: Soak the glass noodles in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking. They soften and cook evenly. Cook each vegetable separately in the wok: this is time-consuming but produces distinctly flavoured components rather than a single mixed flavour. The assembly at the end takes 2 minutes.

content.text: Marinate the beef: toss the sliced beef with 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 teaspoon sugar, and the garlic. Leave for 15 minutes.

Cook the soaked noodles in boiling water for 6 to 8 minutes until tender but with a slight chew. Drain and rinse under cold water. Cut into 15 cm lengths with scissors. Season with 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, and 1 tablespoon sugar. Set aside.

Stir-fry the beef in a little oil over high heat for 2 minutes until cooked. Remove. Stir-fry each vegetable separately (mushrooms, carrot, red pepper, spring onion) for 2 minutes each, seasoning each with a little soy sauce and sesame oil.

Combine everything: the noodles, beef, vegetables, and spinach in a large bowl. Add the remaining soy sauce and sesame oil and toss well. Season to taste. Serve at room temperature or warm, scattered with sesame seeds.

items.cause: Noodles were not rinsed after cooking or not tossed with oil while warm
items.fix: Rinse the noodles immediately after cooking and toss with sesame oil while still warm. If they clump before assembly, toss with a little warm water and sesame oil to separate.
